title: Director Community Based Inclusive Development (CBID)
description:
About CBM CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all. About the role: We are looking for an experienced Director* Community Based Inclusive Development (CBID) to lead CBM’s newly refocused CBID Initiative. In this senior leadership role, you will shape the strategic direction of Inclusive Community Support and Care, Inclusive Education, and Inclusive Livelihood, strengthen CBM’s leadership in disability-inclusive development, and drive greater impact for persons with disabilities through community-based approaches worldwide. This full-time position is only filled locally in one of CBM permanent established entities. (ex: Bensheim (Germany), UK (Cambridge or remote), Nairobi (Kenya), Abuja (Nigeria), Lomé (Togo), Yaoundé (Cameroon), Lusaka (Zambia), Addis Abeba (Ethiopia), Guatemala City, Kampala (Uganda), Niamey (Niger), etc.). Local contractual conditions of the respective country will apply. An expatriation is not intended These are your responsibilities Strategic Leadership Provide overall leadership and management of the CBID Division. Lead, develop and inspire a globally distributed team of CBID and technical advisors. Manage divisional resources, people, budgets and performance to achieve organisational objectives. Position CBM and the CBID work in key global, regional and national processes and alliances which are related to the work of CBID. Develop and implement the global CBID strategy and implementation framework within CBM’s overall strategy. Monitor emerging sector trends and position CBM as a thought leader in community based inclusive development. Grow CBID within CBM as a core pillar of CBM’s strategy. Ensure attractiveness of CBM’s CBID work for Individual and Institutional Donors. Technical Leadership & Quality Develop and maintain technical standards, guidance and tools for CBID programming in the areas of Inclusive. Community Support and Care (ICSC), Inclusive Education, Inclusive Livelihood. Provide guidance to the ICSC team and the advocacy team lead. Directly manage the advisors for Inclusive Livelihood and Inclusive Education. Bring clear approaches (definition, concepts, methods, tools) in the respective technical areas in place. Provide strategic oversight of programme quality. Resource Mobilisation & Organisational Sustainability Contribute to resource mobilisation strategies and donor engagement. Support development of high-quality funding proposals. These are your qualifications Master’s degree in Business Administration, International Development, Disability Studies, Social Sciences or related field. Minimum 10 years of international development experience at managerial level. Extensive expertise in disability-inclusive development and community-based approaches. Ability to define and drive global strategies, translate vision into action, and align diverse stakeholders around common objectives. Proven capability to lead, coach, and develop multicultural and geographically dispersed teams while fostering collaboration, inclusion, and accountability. Professional English; German, French and/or Spanish desirable. Identification with Christian values and the mandate of CBM What we offer A meaningful position with a lot of creative freedom in the world's leading organisation in the field of Disability Inclusive Development A fair salary and other social benefits based on the local conditions in the country you apply for An approachable, agile organisation with self-reliant people in a diverse and collegial team and great team spirit

How to Apply: Please apply exclusively online via our applicant portal (see [APPLY NOW](https://jobs.cbm.org/Director-Community-Based-Inclusive-Development-CBID-eng-f1102.html)). A letter of motivation, CV and relevant (work) references complete your application. We look forward to receiving your application! Your contact person: Ms. Alyzée Brehm-Monbrun We would like to further promote diversity in our teams and therefore welcome applications from people of different ethnic and social backgrounds, religions and world views, different ages and genders, and especially from people with disabilities.

title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
description:
Desired start date: 01/12/2026 Duration of the mission: 6 Months Location: Adwa - Tigray Region SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI) is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms. PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION: Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region). In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors. In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement. SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area. GENERAL OBJECTIVES : The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone. Representation and Internal / external communication: The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep). ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES : Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements. PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS : -Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams. -Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans. -Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components. -Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring. -Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies. -Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context -Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities SECURITY CONSTRAINTS : The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making. YOUR PROFIL : DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required. EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years TECHNICAL SKILLS : Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes. TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection). LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset. SI WILL OFFER YOU : A salaried position: According to experience, starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400. SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment. Breaks: During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked. Insurance package: Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded. Living conditions: Guest House conditions : - There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit. -Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa -Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa : - Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

title: Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Ethiopia October 2026
description:
Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Ethiopia October 2026 Procurement Summary Item Details RFP title Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Supplier type Research or data-collection agency Contract type Framework/on-call arrangement using task orders Geographic scope Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia and South Ethiopia Anticipated contract period October 2026 to September 2027 RFP issue date 5 October 2026 Proposal deadline 12 October 2026 Submission email suppliers@girleffect.org Proposal validity 90 days Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit organization dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change (SBC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 and, since then, has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives. We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood. When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. That’s the Girl Effect. Background Yegna Gize, meaning “Our Time” in Amharic, is a Girl Effect Ethiopia programme that builds on the Yegna brand and its experience of using media, storytelling, role modelling, and community engagement to influence positive social and behavioural change among young people. Yegna Gize focuses specifically on youth economic empowerment, with an emphasis on improving young people's aspirations, mindsets, skills, access to opportunities, and pathways towards employment and entrepreneurship. Over the programme period, Yegna Gize seeks to contribute to improved economic opportunities and livelihood outcomes for young people in Ethiopia by addressing barriers related to employment, entrepreneurship, skills development, social norms, and mindsets. The programme works with young people, schools, communities, government institutions, civil society organisations (CSOs), private-sector actors, role models, and other relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment for youth to pursue viable economic pathways. The programme is implemented across six regions of Ethiopia: Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, Central Ethiopia, Sidama, and South Ethiopia. Through a combination of youth-centred interventions, partnerships, capacity strengthening, communication and social and behavioural change approaches, Yegna Gize aims to strengthen young people's knowledge, skills, confidence, aspirations, networks, and access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities. Key areas of Yegna Gize programming include: Youth employment and transition to work: Supporting young people to access internships, work-based learning, employment opportunities, and other pathways into the labour market. Entrepreneurship and enterprise development: Strengthening entrepreneurial knowledge, business skills, growth mindsets, and access to support for young people interested in starting or growing businesses. Skills and mindset development: Building practical, transferable, entrepreneurial, and employability skills, alongside confidence, aspirations, resilience, and positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship. Peer-to-peer and youth support mechanisms: Establishing and strengthening youth groups and peer-support approaches that enable young people to learn from and support one another. Role modelling and mentorship: Connecting young people with role models, mentors, entrepreneurs, and other influential individuals who can provide inspiration, guidance, and practical exposure to different livelihood pathways. School-based engagement: Working with schools, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship, creativity, growth mindset, career aspirations, and awareness of economic opportunities. Youth-centred media and social and behavioural change communication (SBC): Using Yegna's established multimedia and storytelling platforms to challenge limiting norms, promote positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship, and increase young people's awareness and uptake of available opportunities. Partnerships and systems strengthening: Working with regional and local government structures, CSOs, private-sector actors, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to strengthen the ecosystem supporting youth economic empowerment. Girl Effect works with local partners to contextualise and implement interventions according to regional realities and the needs of young people. The programme therefore combines national-level approaches with locally relevant implementation, allowing interventions to respond to the different economic, social, cultural, and institutional contexts across the six regions. Yegna Gize Programme Impact Study As the programme progresses, Girl Effect Ethiopia intends to commission an independent Impact Study of Yegna Gize to assess the extent to which the programme has contributed to changes in young people's knowledge, skills, attitudes, aspirations, behaviours, access to opportunities, and economic outcomes. The study is expected to generate credible evidence on the effectiveness, relevance, and contribution of Yegna Gize interventions and to identify which approaches are working, for whom, under what conditions, and why. The findings will inform programme learning, adaptation, accountability to stakeholders and donors, and future programming and scale-up decisions. The selected agency will therefore be expected to develop and implement a rigorous and contextually appropriate study methodology that captures both quantitative and qualitative evidence, where appropriate, and considers the diversity of young people, intervention types, implementation approaches, and regional contexts within Yegna Gize. The study should generate actionable evidence and recommendations that can strengthen the programme's contribution to sustainable youth economic empowerment in Ethiopia. Girl Effect is looking to engage a qualified agency to recruit, train, and deploy experienced data collectors across the specified geographic scope, and to manage the full data collection cycle, from fieldwork through to data analysis and submission in line with Girl Effect Ethiopia's tools, sample design, and quality standards. Who You Are The ideal candidate/Agency will: Have demonstrated experience managing field-based data collection for household, community, or individual-level surveys in Ethiopia, ideally on youth, gender, education, livelihoods, or social behaviour change topics. Maintain, or be able to rapidly build, a roster of vetted, experienced enumerators with local language coverage and cultural familiarity across some or all of the six Yegna Gize regions (Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia), including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas. Have hands-on experience with mobile data collection platforms, particularly SurveyCTO, and the ability to train enumerators on tool use ahead of each deployment. Demonstrate robust field supervision and data quality assurance practices — spot-checks, back-checks/call-backs, and real-time progress monitoring against a sample plan. Have in-house or readily available capacity for data cleaning, processing, and first-level quantitative and/or qualitative analysis, with clear documentation of methods. Be able to mobilize and scale data collection teams on short notice against a recurring, on-call task-order structure, without compromising quality or timeliness. Show a genuine commitment to Girl Effect's mission and values, with a demonstrated understanding of child/adolescent safeguarding standards appropriate to research involving youth. Be highly organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple concurrent task orders across different regions. What You will do 2.1 Geographic Coverage Data collection will take place across 6 regions and 60+ woredas, including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas. Exact woreda-level assignments will be shared with the selected agency alongside each task order, together with the corresponding sample size and tool set. 2.2 Sourcing, Vetting, and Onboarding of Data Collectors The agency is responsible for building and maintaining a roster of qualified, experienced data collectors who can be deployed against Girl Effect Ethiopia's task orders. This includes: Recruiting data collectors with relevant prior experience in household or community-level data collection, ideally on similar topics (e.g., health, gender, youth, social behavior change). Ensuring appropriate local language coverage and cultural familiarity for each assigned region/woreda, including pastoralist communities. Verifying qualifications, references, and prior fieldwork experience before onboarding. Maintaining a sufficient bench of vetted collectors to meet fluctuating task-order demand without delays. Ensuring the data collectors are given a functioning tab and are trained on the use of survey CTO. 2.3 Training The agency will organize and deliver training for all data collectors before each deployment, covering: Use of Girl Effect Ethiopia's data collection tools and mobile data collection platform. The sample design and how it translates into fieldwork assignments. Data quality, ethics, consent, and child/adolescent safeguarding protocols appropriate to the population being surveyed. Logistics, reporting lines, and escalation procedures for field issues. Girl Effect Ethiopia will provide technical content on the tools and safeguarding standards; the agency is responsible for organizing, scheduling, and delivering the training itself, and for confirming collector competency before deployment (e.g., through a short practical assessment or pilot/pre-test). 2.4 Deployment Data collectors will be deployed per task order, which Girl Effect Ethiopia will issue for each data collection round/moment. Each task order will specify the woredas/regions, sample size, tools, timeline, and any round-specific instructions. The agency is responsible for: Assigning trained collectors to each task order based on location, language, and availability. Managing collector logistics (travel, accommodation, safety/security arrangements as applicable) within hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas. Providing day-to-day field supervision. 2.5 Data Quality and Timeliness The agency is accountable for the quality and timeliness of data collected under each task order, including: Real-time monitoring of data collection progress against the sample plan and timeline. Quality assurance mechanisms such as spot-checks, back-checks/call-backs, and review of flagged or inconsistent entries. Prompt escalation and resolution of fieldwork issues (e.g., inaccessible households, refusals, tool malfunctions) that could affect data quality or timelines. Regular progress reporting to Girl Effect Ethiopia (proposed: daily or weekly, to be agreed) showing completion rates by woreda/region. 2.6 Data Analysis and Submission Upon completion of each round of data collection, the agency will: Clean and process the collected data. Conduct analysis as specified in the task order. Submit the final clean dataset (in the agreed format), any cleaning/analysis syntax or code, and a summary report to Girl Effect Ethiopia within the timeline specified in the task order. Responsibilities The Hiring Organization and the selected Consultant/agency will have the following division of roles: Activity Girl Effect Ethiopia Contracted Agency Data collection tools & sampling frame Provides (already designed) Reviews & confirms understanding Data collector recruitment Sets qualification criteria; final sign-off Sources, screens candidates Training Provides technical/content input; approves training plan Organizes and delivers logistics Task orders Issues task order per round/moment Deploys collectors against task order Fieldwork supervision Spot-checks and technical backstopping Day-to-day field supervision Data quality assurance Defines quality standards; conducts audits Implements real-time QA checks Timeliness tracking Reviews progress dashboards Reports daily/weekly progress against timeline Data cleaning & analysis Reviews and validates Cleans, processes, and produces first-level analysis Submission Receives final dataset & report Submits clean dataset, syntax/code, and summary report Deliverables Specific deliverables for the duration of the engagement will include:- Roster of vetted, trained data collectors, updated and available on an ongoing basis. Training plan and completion records for each deployment. Field deployment plan per task order (collector-to-woreda assignment). Data collection progress reports (per agreed frequency) per task order. Quality assurance reports (back-check/spot-check findings and resolutions). Clean, validated datasets with accompanying documentation. First-level analysis and summary report per task order. Deliverables will be accepted when they meet the applicable task order, agreed quality standards and Girl Effect’s written feedback. The agency must correct substantiated quality issues attributable to its work at no additional fee. Expected Commitment This engagement is structured as a framework/on-call arrangement: the agency will be expected to mobilize data collectors on a per-task-order basis over the contract period between October 2026 and September 2027, with the frequency and scale of rounds varying according to program needs. Each task order will specify its own scope, sample, and timeline. Management The Consultant will have a primary point of contact within the Evidence & Insight team. Procurement Timeline Terms of Reference Published: Oct 5, 2026 Deadline for Proposal Submission: Oct 12, 2026 Proposal Submission Interested Consultant/agency should submit a maximum 10-page proposal that includes the following: Technical Proposal A CV or organizational profile outlining previous work and experience relevant to field data collection, enumerator training and management, and data analysis, particularly within the Ethiopian context and specifically highlighting experience across the Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, and/or South Ethiopia regions, including hard-to-reach or pastoralist areas where applicable. A brief overview of your understanding of Girl Effect's mission and the objectives of this assignment, and your proposed methodology — covering enumerator sourcing and vetting, training approach, field supervision structure, data quality assurance mechanisms (e.g., spot-checks, back-checks), and your approach to data cleaning and first-level analysis. Examples of at least two to three previous data collection and/or analysis assignments completed within the specified regions, demonstrating comparable scale, topic area, and quality outcomes. Reference — Provide at least three references for similar contracts with a description of the service provided, the value of the contract, and the contract periods of performance. Financial Proposal Please provide your proposed fee in ETB , including the total cost for impact the study assignment, along with a detailed breakdown by deliverable, aligned with the activities outlined in the Scope of Work for the region(s) you are applying to cover. Ensure that all applicable taxes are clearly itemized in your proposal. Evaluation Criteria Evaluation will follow three stages: Pre-screening Technical evaluation Financial evaluation Technical Evaluation – 70% No. Technical Evaluation Criterion Weight 1. Relevant Organizational Experience in Impact Evaluation, Research and Data Collection 15% 2. Understanding of Yegna Gize Programme and Assignment / TOR 10% 3. Proposed Research Methodology and Impact Evaluation Approach 20% 4. Sampling, Fieldwork and Data Collection Strategy 10% 5. Technical Capacity, Quality Assurance, Team Expertise and Operational Feasibility 15% Total Technical Score 70% Value for Money / Financial Competitiveness – 30% The financial scoring is based on the total evaluated cost , while also checking whether the proposed budget is sufficiently detailed and realistic across key cost categories such as personnel, training, fieldwork, travel/logistics, data management, analysis and reporting. GE is not liable for any cost incurred during the award/contract preparation, submission, or negotiation of the award/contract. All submitted documentation and/or materials shall become and remain the property of GE, and Technical & Financial proposals will need to be submitted as a separate document. Girl Effect may request clarifications, interviews, presentations, reference checks, due diligence or best-and-final offers. The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected. General and Commercial Terms Framework and task orders: The successful agency will sign Girl Effect’s applicable framework agreement. Work may begin only after an authorised task order has been issued. The framework does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work. Contracting and Payment: The successful agency will sign Girl Effect’s applicable agreement. Payments will be linked to the satisfactory delivery and written acceptance of agreed milestones and receipt of a correct invoice. Girl Effect may withhold acceptance pending correction of material quality issues. Pricing, taxes and expenses: Prices must be quoted in Ethiopian Birr and remain firm during the proposal-validity period. Taxes and approved reimbursable expenses must be itemised separately. Girl Effect will deduct or account for taxes as required by Ethiopian law. Unapproved costs will not be reimbursed. Intellectual property and data ownership: Subject to the final agreement, Girl Effect will own the commissioned outputs, research data, instruments, documentation and analysis produced under the engagement. The agency may not reuse, publish or disclose these materials without Girl Effect’s prior written approval. Confidentiality and data protection: The agency must use personal and confidential information only for this assignment, apply appropriate technical and organisational safeguards, promptly report incidents and securely return or delete data when instructed. Safeguarding, ethics and conduct: The agency and all assigned personnel must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, informed-consent, ethical research, anti-fraud, information-security and supplier-conduct requirements. Required checks and training must be completed before deployment. Personnel and subcontracting: Changes to key personnel and the use of subcontractors require Girl Effect’s prior written approval. The agency will remain responsible for the quality, conduct and performance of all subcontracted work. Conflicts of interest: Bidders must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest. Equal opportunity: Girl Effect is committed to equal opportunity and encourages submissions from organisations with strong local knowledge and diverse professional and cultural backgrounds. Right to award: Girl Effect may seek clarification, negotiate, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, award all or part of the requirement, appoint more than one agency or make no award. Girl Effect will not reimburse proposal-preparation or negotiation costs. Proposal validity: Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

How to Apply: ### **How To Apply** Email the technical and financial proposals as separate attachments to: **suppliers@girleffect.org.** Applications must be received by **12th October 2026.** Use the subject line: **Yegna Gize Field Research Services –Ethiopia** Submissions that do not follow the stated application process may not be evaluated. Only successful bidder or bidders will be notified.

title: Partnerships and Private Sector Engagement Manager Ethiopia
description:
What we’re looking for: NRC Ethiopia is looking for an experienced Partnerships and Private Sector Engagement Manager to lead and strengthen how we build, manage, and grow meaningful partnerships. In this role, you will play a key part in developing and implementing NRC Ethiopia’s Partnership Strategy and related SOPs, ensuring that our partnership approach is aligned with NRC’s vision, strategic priorities, policies, and commitment to localisation. You will help create a consistent and coordinated approach to partnerships across the Country Office and, where needed, Area Offices. You will build and maintain strong relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders, including civil society organisations, private sector actors, academic institutions, and public authorities. You will also oversee the full lifecycle of formal partnerships - from due diligence and partner selection to capacity assessments, agreement management, compliance monitoring, and audits. Working closely with Specialists, Area Programme Managers, Project Managers, and Finance teams, you will ensure that partnerships are well managed, compliant, and focused on delivering quality programmes. A key part of your role will be to support and strengthen the capacity of NRC’s partners. You will ensure that partners understand relevant donor requirements, compliance regulations, reporting deadlines, and NRC procedures, while providing practical support to help them meet these requirements. Beyond partnership management, you will also help strengthen the culture of meaningful and equitable partnerships within NRC Ethiopia. You will advise colleagues and leadership on strategic partnership decisions, promote knowledge and capacity sharing, and contribute to advancing localisation across our programmes. This is an important role for someonewho believes that strong partnerships are more than agreements on paper. They are relationships built on trust, shared responsibility, mutual learning, and a common commitment to achieving better outcomes for the people we serve. If you are an Ethiopian National, and an experienced partnership professional who enjoys connecting people, organisations, and ideas - and who can turn partnerships into practical results - we would like to hear from you. Please download a more detailed JOB DESCRIPTION for more specific duties and responsibilities. What you will bring: 3-5 years of experience in working in a humanitarian/recovery/human rights or development context. University degree combined with relevant professional background. Knowledge of humanitarian principles. Experience in managing and implementing programs in humanitarian contexts. Ability to work independently and proactively. title: 23257 Chief Migration Health Officer (P)
description:
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM), and the technical supervision of the Regional Health Assessment Programme Coordinator (RHAPC) and in coordination with the Head of Programmes and the Regional Migration Health Specialist for your region, the Chief Migration Health Officer will be responsible for the development, implementation, and management of the Health Assessment and other health programmes. Responsibilities and Accountabilities Health Assessment Portfolio Organize and supervise the migration health assessment process to fulfil the technical requirements of the resettlement countries in the areas of: 1. Medical examinations 2. Imaging 3. Laboratory testing 4. Vaccinations 5. TB management 6. Treatment and referrals 7. Pre-departure procedures and medical movements 8. Documentation, certification and information transmission 9. Other technical areas as may be required Ensure that the infrastructure and equipment of Health Assessment Programme (HAP) premises meet professional standards of quality and safety and are sufficient and adequate for the provision of the services. Ensure that human resources and HAP organizational structure are sufficient and adequate for the planned levels of health assessments and that the staff have the necessary qualifications and skills. Establish a sufficient network of external human resources, such as consultants and medical escorts, to support the health assessment process and travel assistance. In coordination with the Human Resource Unit, ensure that all medical personnel maintain valid licenses to practice. Ensure that the regulatory government authorities are informed about IOM’s health activities and that the IOM medical facilities have obtained approval to provide health assessments and related services. Establish and maintain efficient, client-centered procedures and ensure a high level of integrity at all stages of the HAP process, including client information and appointment system, payment, registration, pre- and post-test counselling, examination, testing, treatment and referrals, submission of health assessment results, pre-departure and other procedures. Establish and maintain a system enabling clients to provide feedback. Establish and maintain a system of quality improvement for each service area. Undertake quality control activities on a regular basis; practice observation and regular supervisory visits to all facilities/teams involved in the health assessment operations. desk audits and use self-assessment tools. Use data analysis and a web reporting system to monitor performance indicators. Ensure implementation of the global IOM Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); create and implement country-specific SOPs for each service area. Ensure proper reporting and management of incidents according to the Guidance Note for Incident Management. Incorporate additional public health interventions in the HAP context. Such interventions may include surveillance for communicable diseases, outbreak preparedness and response, health education and health promotion, public health services for host communities, liaison with public health institutions, and other activities. Supervise health and non-health staff as well as external consultants involved in the health assessment process; ensure that performance evaluations for health staff are completed in a timely manner. Ensure that all staff are aware of the IOM Standards of Conduct under Article 42, and continuously reinforce these standards. Inform in due time the COM and the IOM Ethics Committee of any issues regarding staff misconduct. Establish the HAP staff development strategy and ensure that the appropriate plan is implemented. Within that plan, apart from attendance at external educational events, initiate, organize, and deliver various professional in-house trainings. Liaise with external service providers to negotiate agreements in coordination with the Resource Management Officer (RMO). To the extent possible, exercise quality control over outsourced services and take corrective measures if necessary. Liaise with relevant partners at government level, immigration and health authorities of the receiving countries, as well as other international UN and non-UN agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), donor community and national partners. Maintain confidentiality and security of migration health data in accordance with the IOM Data Protection Principles. Organize systematic collection, processing, and analyses of migration health data. Ensure data quality. Provide periodic, as well as ad hoc reporting to the Migration Health Division (MHD) for Migration Health (MH) activities. Oversee the financial aspects of the health programmes in close coordination with the mission's finance staff: supervise budget preparation and ensure monitoring of MH projects, suggest adjustments and cost-effective solutions, and review financial reports. Provide oversight and coordinate procurement of medical equipment, vaccines, medications, and other medical supplies in coordination with the resource management unit. Organize and supervise activities of mobile medical teams, if applicable. Other Health Activities In coordination with the Head of Office (HOO)/COM, reinforce partnerships and liaise with the Migration Health (MH) sector with the Ministry of Health, health institutions and academia, as well as other relevant leading agencies. Incorporate multi-sectoral approaches to partnerships, as well as capitalize on IOM strengths across all service areas within the overall framework of IOM’s 12-point Strategy adopted by IOM Member States (June 2007). Conceptualize, develop and implement appropriate migration health-related projects that may benefit migrants, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities as well as conflict/natural disaster affected population in coordination with relevant Units, the Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs) and other colleagues. Facilitate the integration of health assessment activities into the overall migration-related programming of the Country Office through close collaboration with the various units at the Country Office level. Advise IOM colleagues on the link between the Health Assessment Programme with the two other core MHD programme areas - Health Promotion and Assistance to Migrants, and Migration Health Assistance to Crisis-Affected Populations. Identify opportunities for expanding migration health activities and programmes by informing embassies and consulates of IOM’s migration health work and lobbying for IOM Migration Health Assessment Centres (MHACs) becoming panel sites for Migration Health Assessments (MHA), responding to announcements for calls for proposals by drafting project concept notes and/or proposals and liaising with UN agencies and the Ministry of Health to identify project development opportunities. Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Required Qualifications and Experience Education University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution with preferred specializations: internal medicine and its subspecialties, Paediatrics, Anaesthesiology, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynaecology; and a minimum of nine years of relevant professional experience, of which at least three years of managerial responsibilities; or, University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution with preferred specializations: internal medicine and its subspecialties, Paediatrics, Anaesthesiology, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, plus Master’s Degree in Community or Public Health, Medical Specialization in Infectious Diseases, Tropical Medicine, or other related fields from an accredited academic institution, with seven years of relevant professional experience, of which at least three years of managerial responsibilities. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Professional continuous clinical experience, preferably in a multidisciplinary hospital setting or at IOM/similar international clinic context; Experience in Migration Health Assessments; Demonstrated progressive experience in health programme management; Experience in project development, management, and report writing; and, Experience in migration health emergency response is an asset. Skills Effective managerial and leadership skills; Proven abilities to establish partnerships with government institutions, health institutions, and other partners; Knowledge of public health; Demonstrable knowledge of patient safety and infection prevention and control; Organizational skills; and, Communication skills. Languages For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage. Promote transparency, responsiveness, and power-sharing through strengthened accountability practices. 4. title: RESPONSABLE DU BUREAU DE PLAIDOYER ET DE LIAISON AUPRÈS DE L’UNION AFRICAINE, Oxfam en Afrique
description:
Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée de 2 ans Grade interne : B1, International Rémunération : conforme à la grille salariale d’Oxfam International. Cette offre comprend les avantages sociaux de base ainsi que les prestations globales applicables au personnel recruté à l’international et relocalisé.Nous considérons que les modalités de travail flexibles sont essentielles pour bâtir le Secrétariat de demain. Nous sommes donc disposés à échanger avec vous sur les modalités susceptibles de vous convenir. Le poste Oxfam en Afrique recherche une personne expérimentée, dotée d’un leadership reconnu et d’un forte capacité d’influence, pour diriger son Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine (UA), basé à Addis-Abeba. En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. Le Secrétariat d’Oxfam International participe également au Mécanisme interorganisations de divulgation des inconduites (Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). Conformément à ce dispositif, si une personne candidate a précédemment travaillé pour une autre organisation membre, nous solliciterons auprès de cette organisation des informations concernant toute constatation d’exploitation sexuelle, d’abus sexuels et/ou de harcèlement sexuel survenue pendant son emploi, ainsi que tout incident qui faisait encore l’objet d’une enquête au moment de son départ. En soumettant sa candidature, la personne candidate confirme avoir pris connaissance de cette procédure de recrutement.

How to Apply: **Comment postuler** Si vous souhaitez influencer les politiques continentales et renforcer l’engagement auprès de l’Union africaine afin de favoriser des changements durables en Afrique, nous vous invitons à postuler. Veuillez soumettre un CV à jour et une lettre de motivation via ce lien [https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360](https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360) , en démontrant clairement en quoi votre profil répond aux critères essentiels définis dans la fiche de poste de Responsable du Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine. title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia. The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights. Responsibilities Data Collection & Research Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas. Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning. Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights. Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion. Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness. Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes. Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information. Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings. Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks. Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. Reporting & Collaboration Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions. Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions. Vital Strategies’ priorities are driven by the greatest potential to improve and save lives.
